🚇 AI Idea Flow · 2012 → 2026

From AlexNet to Today: How Ideas Flowed and Merged

Read AI's last fourteen years like a metro map. Each coloured line is a research area, each station is a landmark paper, and glowing links carry ideas from where they began to what they made possible. Where a link crosses to another line, two fields merged into something new. Click any station to open its family tree.

🌌 See it in 3D
Jump to:
Station = a landmark idea Interchange = built on two or more fields Flow: origin → later idea (left to right) ★ prize-recognised Click a line's name on the left to focus it
How to read this map: stations are the paper cards from the AI Research Progress Through the Years articles, so the map shows what that series covers, not all of AI. The links are our editorial reading of each paper's lineage — direct building blocks, methods it combined, or ideas it replaced — taken from each card's "What they found" and "Why it matters". Influence is often shared and debatable, so read a link as "strongly influenced", not as a formal citation. The lines are broad research areas we assigned, and many papers could sit on two. "Key ideas" is a curated subset; the family tree always shows every link, including ideas from before 2012.
